submissions.findingTextShort: The existing systematic review supports only limited, stress-context cognition evidence rather than generic L-Tyrosine enhancement.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 32093203 reviewed dietary supplements and cognition in healthy young adults and military-relevant populations. Most included research was rated low quality, and the review's favorable Tyrosine interpretation was concentrated on cognitive performance when personnel were sleep deprived. The existing approved receipt therefore supports a bounded stressor-specific proposition, not routine baseline cognition, ADHD treatment, or generic daily focus enhancement.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy young adults and military-relevant populations represented in the systematic review.
submissions.usageContext: Primarily sleep-deprivation or operational-stress cognition context; existing canonical source reused.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Most included research was low quality and the review did not establish broad enhancement across ordinary rested conditions.

submissions.findingTextShort: A controlled sleep-deprivation study found task-specific cognitive and motor benefits from acute high-dose Tyrosine.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 12887140 evaluated Tyrosine 150 mg/kg after overnight sleep deprivation in healthy young men alongside placebo and stimulant comparators. Tyrosine improved selected tasks including running memory, logical reasoning, mathematical processing, tracking and visual vigilance after sleep-deprivation-related decrements, but effects were not universal across the battery and were less broad than D-amphetamine. This supports an acute impairment-context signal rather than a general nootropic effect.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy young men studied after overnight sleep deprivation.
submissions.usageContext: Single acute experimental dose of 150 mg/kg; not a consumer maintenance regimen.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Task-specific effects and an extreme experimental stress context limit generalization to rested users or chronic use. Draft-only pending source governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A very small cold-exposure trial found Tyrosine reversed the working-memory condition most impaired by acute cold stress.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 8029265 used a double-blind placebo-controlled crossover design in eight men exposed to 4 degrees C or 22 degrees C after 150 mg/kg L-Tyrosine or placebo. Cold exposure impaired delayed matching accuracy under placebo, and Tyrosine improved performance at the longest delay interval most affected by cold. The finding is a small acute environmental-stress signal and cannot establish routine cognition enhancement outside cold-induced impairment.
submissions.populationContext: Eight male volunteers during acute laboratory cold exposure.
submissions.usageContext: Acute 150 mg/kg experimental dose before cold stress; working-memory endpoint only.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Very small sample, acute laboratory exposure, and outcome specificity sharply limit external validity. Draft-only pending source governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized trial found 2 g Tyrosine worsened cognitive flexibility under high cognitive load rather than improving it.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 31521870 randomized 70 healthy volunteers in a double-blind placebo-controlled experiment using 2 g Tyrosine with low or high cognitive load before repeat cognitive-flexibility testing. Contrary to the expected benefit, Tyrosine worsened cognitive flexibility in the high-load condition. This negative result demonstrates that demanding-task evidence is not uniformly favorable and must remain a first-class counterweight to broad focus or resilience language.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy adult volunteers under experimentally manipulated cognitive load.
submissions.usageContext: Single 2 g dose; cognitive-flexibility outcome rather than sleep-deprivation or cold-stress recovery.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The trial did not measure a physiological stress marker, and the result should not be generalized to every task or exposure. Draft-only pending source governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A small placebo-controlled narcolepsy trial found little objective or overall clinical benefit from 9 g/day L-Tyrosine.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 2572797 tested L-Tyrosine 9 g/day versus placebo in ten people with narcolepsy and cataplexy. Only three of 28 subjective mood/arousal scales differed, while daytime drowsiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, nighttime sleep, overall clinical response, multiple sleep latency, speed and attention did not differ significantly. This disease-population null/mixed evidence must not be repurposed as support for generic alertness or sleep treatment.
submissions.populationContext: Ten people with narcolepsy and cataplexy.
submissions.usageContext: 9 g/day disease-treatment trial; not a wellness or routine cognitive-enhancement regimen.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The study is very small and historical, but its null objective/clinical outcomes remain relevant negative evidence. Draft-only pending source governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: The live profile's specific medication and thyroid cautions are not independently reconstructable from its single cognition-review receipt.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The current L-Tyrosine profile exposes one approved cognition systematic review and one context-specific cognition claim while public safety fields separately name MAOI, hyperthyroidism or Graves disease, levodopa, stimulant medication, and thyroid-medication review. Those safety propositions are not independently reconstructable from the visible claim/source ledger. They require dedicated safety or pharmacology receipts before governed promotion; the efficacy studies staged here do not establish or strengthen those interaction claims.
submissions.usageContext: Repository provenance gap only; no interaction conclusion or public safety mutation is made here.
submissions.safetyContext: Medication and thyroid cautions require independent source-specific validation before consumer-facing use.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The cautions may be valid, but this research record deliberately separates lack of receipt from evidence of absence or evidence of harm.
